# Exact failures of depth quasiconcavity along shadow systems

A shadow system here is C_t=conv{a_i+t v_i e}, with one fixed direction e.
The conjectural inequality maxdepth(C_t)>=min(maxdepth(C_0),maxdepth(C_1))
fails both continuously and with one integer coordinate.

## 1. A four-point continuous planar example

Let n=0,d=2 and let C_t be the convex hull of

    (-1,-1), (-1,1), (1,-1+2t), (1,1-2t),     0<=t<=1.

Every moving velocity is vertical, and every C_t has nonempty interior.
Both C_0 and C_1 are the square [-1,1]^2, whose maximum halfspace depth is
1/2: the center bisects every through-center halfspace, while for every point
one of two complementary halfspaces through it has at most half the area.
At t=1/2 the body is the triangle conv{(-1,-1),(-1,1),(1,0)}. Its exact maximum
depth is gamma_2=4/9. Thus quasiconcavity fails strictly, despite full-dimensional
bodies at all times. The collision of two moving vertices is allowed by the
standard shadow-system definition.

## 2. A fixed-integer vertical example with affine interval fibers

Let n=d=1 and P={0,1,2,3}. At the two endpoints take interval fibers

    A: [0,12], [-3,24], [-1,28], [6,32],
    B: [0,21], [-9,24], [-3,21], [7,14].

Match the lower and upper endpoint at each fixed integer z and move each
vertically with its affine endpoint velocity. Every intermediate lower
sequence remains convex and every intermediate upper sequence remains
concave, because these are linear slope inequalities valid at both ends.
Consequently the actual integer fibers of C_t are exactly the interpolated
intervals. No replacement of a fiber hull by a different union is used.

The exact certificates in candidate 94a1565e143d393e
and ../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_minkowski_depth_obstruction.py prove

    maxdepth(A)>=20/47,
    maxdepth(B)>=147/340,
    maxdepth(C_(1/2))=63/179.

Both endpoint lower bounds are strictly greater than the midpoint value.
Here C_(1/2) has half the interval coordinates of the certified fiberwise
Minkowski sum; this common continuous scaling preserves normalized depth.
Thus the same fully rational certificate is also an exact fixed-integer
shadow-system obstruction. It does not rely on changing projection indices.

These counterexamples close global shadow-system quasiconcavity as an
extremal mechanism. The exact local circuit-quantile comparison from
candidate a0fdd477aa859374 remains valid; no unproved monotonicity
is inferred from ordinary volume convexity along a shadow system.
